changes.before: The first time labor could be handed to something that ran on its own. The machine is the second.
changes.after: An early way to hand over some of the heavy work. Training, guidance, and care still belonged to people.

changes.before: The two machines this whole book is about: one that grows the food, one that builds the house. The pieces already exist; the work is putting them in your neighbors' hands.
changes.after: The two machines this whole book is about: one that grows the food, one that builds the house. The pieces are arriving. The work is putting them in your neighbors' hands.

changes.before: The epidemic, as the doctors saw it. Two hundred years later we hand this exact picture to children as the cure for their screens.
changes.after: The epidemic, as its critics saw it. Two hundred years later we hand this exact picture to children as the cure for their screens.

changes.before: Pacific madrone, mid-shed. It burns to the ground and comes back from the root.
changes.after: Pacific madrone, mid-shed. It can burn to the ground and come back from the root.

changes.before: The event horizon of M87. Past a certain line, there is no going back.
changes.after: The shadow of the black hole M87\*. Past a certain line, there's no going back.

changes.before: Robotic arms assembling a car body
changes.after: Robotic arms in an interactive Jaguar assembly exhibit at Thinktank, Birmingham

changes.before: Robotic arms at work. The structural automation of labor, already routine.
changes.after: Robotic arms in Thinktank's interactive Jaguar assembly exhibit. A demonstration of industrial automation.

changes.before: Falcon Heavy demo mission. The exodus hardware is already flying.
changes.after: Falcon Heavy demo mission. The first rungs of a very long ladder.

changes.before: The Sun, via NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory. The only income the planet has.
changes.after: The Sun, via NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory. The dominant energy income of everything alive on Earth.

changes.before: A squat black cast-iron wood stove with the door open, one cracked firebrick visible inside
changes.after: A squat black wood stove with the door open, one cracked firebrick visible inside

changes.before: The Fisher. Eighty pounds of steel, one cracked firebrick. Older than him.
changes.after: The Fisher. Four hundred pounds of steel, one cracked firebrick. Older than him.

changes.before: Pixel-art portraits of the co-op: Elijah, Marta, Priya, and Denny
changes.after: Pixel-art portraits of the co-op: Elijah the ex-tech worker with his notebook, Marta the fabricator in her welding apron, Priya the soil scientist with a broadfork, and Denny the former logistics worker

changes.before: A 1929 newspaper advertisement headlined "Taking Liberties With Folks' Habits," showing a large robot shouldering aside a weeping cherub at a harp while a dog howls, above columns of argument signed by the American Federation of Musicians
changes.after: A robot shoulders aside a weeping cherub at a harp while a dog howls at it

changes.before: Exhibitors Herald-World, November 16, 1929. "Is the Robot such good company he can 'hog the whole show?'"
changes.after: Exhibitors Herald-World, November 16, 1929. The union asks whether the Robot is good enough company to hog the whole show.

changes.before: A 1930 newspaper advertisement headlined "Is the Robot Fooling YOU?", showing a robot among classical muses holding a banner reading CANNED MUSIC IN THEATERS, with a mail-in coupon enrolling the reader in the Music Defense League
changes.after: A robot stands among classical muses holding a banner reading CANNED MUSIC IN THEATERS

changes.before: Gary. Stayed informed. Couldn't fix a fence.
changes.after: Gary. Stayed informed.

changes.before: The Cognitive Extraction Engine: raw attention is harvested by infinite scroll and notifications, depleting the prefrontal cortex, producing systemic suggestibility, and ending in loss of physical agency
changes.after: A conceptual sequence: scrolling and alerts compete with a chosen task, repeated switches leave work waiting, and less time may remain for that task. This is an illustration, not a neurological model.

changes.before: The Cognitive Extraction Engine. Attention goes in at the top; agency comes out the bottom, and the platform keeps the difference.
changes.after: The Cognitive Extraction Engine. A picture of diverted time, not a measurement of brain chemistry.

changes.before: The Cognitive Fragmentation Curve: a graph of cognitive depth over one hour, showing a twenty-minute climb to deep-focus baseline, then repeated algorithmic interrupts, each recovery peaking lower than the last
changes.after: An illustrative curve of attention on a task rising, dropping at interruptions, and recovering between them. The axes have no measured scale and the curve makes no claim about a fixed recovery time.

changes.before: The Cognitive Fragmentation Curve. Above roughly three interrupts an hour, the curve never touches baseline again.
changes.after: One possible pattern of interrupted work. A conceptual sketch, not measured data or a universal recovery curve.

changes.before: The Cognitive Firewall Pipeline: the high-entropy digital web passes through strict batch processing, then text-only synthesis, and emerges as deep physical execution
changes.after: A suggested attention routine: check incoming information in scheduled windows, make notes, then return to a chosen task. This is a practical proposal, not a measured change in entropy or agency.

changes.before: The Cognitive Firewall Pipeline. Entropy falls left to right; agency rises.
changes.after: The Cognitive Firewall Pipeline. A routine to try and adjust around the work and people who need you.

changes.before: Two architectures for the same brain. The stream keeps you reactive; the batch keeps you sovereign.
changes.after: Two architectures for the same brain. The stream keeps you reactive; the batch keeps you in charge.

changes.before: Trust network topologies: a star topology where every node depends on one hub that can fail, versus a mesh topology where every node connects to several neighbors and damage becomes a detour
changes.after: Illustrative network topologies: a star depends on one hub, while the mesh has alternate connections that may provide a route around a failure.

changes.before: Star versus mesh. In the star, the hub's failure is everyone's failure; in the mesh, damage is a routing problem.
changes.after: Star versus mesh. The star loses its links when the hub fails. The mesh can reroute if another working path remains.

changes.before: Two supply lines compared: a long fragile global chain versus a short hyper-local loop
changes.after: Two supply lines compared side by side: a long fragile global chain of raw material, overseas factory, ocean freight and last-mile truck, versus a short hyper-local loop of local material, neighborhood factory, and you

changes.before: Not decentralization for its own sake. A shorter line you can hold in your head.
changes.after: Not decentralization for its own sake. A shorter line: one you can hold in your head, that depends on your neighbors' hands instead of strangers far away.

changes.before: You do not deglobalize a city by walling it off. You ring it with municipalities that produce what it cannot, which is also where the good jobs are.
changes.after: You don't deglobalize a city by walling it off. You ring it with towns that produce what it can't, which is also where the good jobs are.

changes.before: The CNC Autonomous Bed. Every plant is a coordinate; the machine tends the whole grid from one rail.
changes.after: The CNC bed. Every plant is a coordinate; the machine tends the grid from one rail.

changes.before: The Greenhouse Automation Bus. Sensors in on I2C, 12V actuators out on GPIO relays, PID loops in the middle.
changes.after: The greenhouse bus. Sensors in on I2C, low-voltage actuators out on relays, control loops in the middle.

changes.before: Model collapse generation by generation: a wide, rich human-data distribution at Generation 0 narrows to a piled-up mean at Generation 1 and finally to a single degenerate spike at Generation 5
changes.after: Schematic model collapse: a broad distribution narrows over successive generations. The generation labels illustrate the process, not a measured timetable for language models.

changes.before: Model collapse across one training lineage. The rich tails, the edge cases, the genius, are pruned first and gone by Generation 5.
changes.after: A simplified picture of model collapse across one training lineage, not a forecast of which generation fails. Rare cases can disappear first.

changes.before: The Algorithmic Judo pipeline: a high-utility off-grid tech core wrapped in an outrage or tragedy narrative hook is scored viral by the algorithm and delivered to a human target who unlocks the core
changes.after: A proposed publishing path: useful instructions become part of a true story, travel through a feed, and reach a reader who can use them. Reach isn't guaranteed.

changes.before: Algorithmic Judo. A dry manual scores near zero; wrapped in a human story, the algorithm carries it for you.
changes.after: Algorithmic judo: give a useful manual a human entry point. Distribution still depends on the platform and the people who encounter it.

changes.before: The Split-Loop Thermal Exchange. Pull the heat straight off the silicon and dump it outside, instead of paying an AC unit to fight your own server.
changes.after: The split loop. Pull the heat off the silicon and dump it outside, instead of paying an air conditioner to fight your own server.

changes.before: The Semi-Autonomous CSA. Automated nodes run at roughly 300% of their own need; the surplus carries whoever cannot produce.
changes.after: The semi-autonomous CSA. Whatever surplus the nodes produce goes to the neighbors who can't. The point is distribution, not a guaranteed yield.

changes.before: Solar on an outbuilding. The Shouse Grid starts with one roof.
changes.after: Solar on an outbuilding. The shouse grid starts with one roof.

changes.before: The Double-Wide Shell. Two one-trip containers, one surgical cut, 640 square feet of open span.
changes.after: The double-wide shell, in plan. Two containers, one room, and a steel skeleton where the walls used to be.

changes.before: The Thermal Barrier Layer: wall section showing heat from the exterior hitting the 2 mm steel wall, being absorbed by 75 mm of closed-cell spray foam rated R-21, and blocked before the interior wood panel
changes.after: Illustrative wall section: steel, closed-cell foam, and interior finish. Insulation reduces heat flow; joints, penetrations, moisture control, and fire protection still need a complete design.

changes.before: The thermal barrier in section. Foam bonded to bare steel: vapor-sealed, condensation-proof, and the heat stays outside.
changes.after: The thermal barrier in section. A continuous insulation and air barrier helps keep warm, moist indoor air away from cold metal.

changes.before: Interior of an abandoned shopping mall
changes.after: An abandoned bar inside an older shopping mall in Haifa

changes.before: A dead mall. Gradually, then suddenly.
changes.after: An abandoned bar in an older shopping mall in Haifa. Gradually, then suddenly.

changes.before: The Logistic Shockwave. A just-in-time system has no buffer to absorb the blow, so the blow travels straight through to the shelves.
changes.after: The logistic shockwave. A system with no buffer passes every blow straight through to the shelves.

changes.before: Centralized versus decentralized mesh communications: a single tower serving three users fails entirely when broken, while a mesh of nodes routes around any dead node
changes.after: Two example networks: users dependent on one tower lose their link when it fails; a mesh with several surviving radio paths can pass messages around a failed node.

changes.before: Two topologies for a town. The tower is a single point of failure; the mesh treats damage as a routing problem.
changes.after: Two topologies for a town. A mesh can route around damage only where another usable path remains.

changes.before: The Cooperative Land Trust Firewall: the speculative real estate market's attempts to buy or foreclose are blocked by a legal shield; inside the trust, the land is held in perpetuity and leased to community stewards on a 99-year ground lease
changes.after: Community land trust structure: a nonprofit holds land under resale restrictions and members hold improvements under a long ground lease. Taxes, debt, and governance duties remain; the structure doesn't guarantee protection from foreclosure.

changes.before: The CLT firewall. Split the title, and the market can no longer reach the dirt.
changes.after: The land-trust idea. Split the title, and the speculative market has a much harder time reaching the dirt.

changes.before: The Soil Food Web. A biological refinery running on sunlight: the plants feed the web that feeds the plants.
changes.after: The soil food web. Sunlight feeds the plants, the plants feed the microbes, and the microbes help feed the plants.

changes.before: Server racks. Code and media scale while you sleep.
changes.after: Server racks. A useful record can travel beyond the people who made it.

changes.before: The Sneakernet Cycle. A terabyte walks across town in a pocket, and nobody upstream ever sees a packet.
changes.after: The sneakernet cycle. A library walks across town in a pocket.

changes.before: A pixel-art specimen board of the field kit: photobioreactor, grow tower, LoRa node, solar and battery, 3D printer, CNC plasma table, walk-behind tractor, cyberdeck
changes.after: A pixel-art specimen board of the field kit: a photobioreactor, a vertical grow tower, a LoRa mesh node, a solar-and-battery rig, a 3D printer, a CNC plasma table, a walk-behind tractor, and a cyberdeck

changes.before: The field kit. Every one of these already exists, and a person with modest money and stubbornness can own the lot.
changes.after: The field kit. Every one of these already exists, and a person with modest money and stubbornness can get their hands on most of it.

changes.before: A DIY 3D-printed photobioreactor growing green algae with a Raspberry Pi board
changes.after: A DIY 3D-printed photobioreactor: a clear vessel of bright green algae culture on a printed frame with a Raspberry Pi board and status light

changes.before: The closed algae fish-food loop: fish, grow beds, dry and grind, photobioreactor, back to fish
changes.after: The closed algae fish-food loop drawn as a cycle: fish tank to grow beds to dry-and-grind to photobioreactor and back to the fish as home-made food

changes.before: Grow the fish food too, and the last store-bought input drops out. The loop closes.
changes.after: Grow the fish food too, and one more store-bought input drops out.

changes.before: Anatomy of a hyper-local mesh node: a waterproof Pelican case containing a 5-watt solar panel feeding two salvaged 18650 batteries feeding an ESP32 LoRa chip, with a tuned antenna broadcasting to the next node on 915 or 868 MHz
changes.after: Illustrative mesh-node hardware: a solar panel, charger and protected battery matched to one another, a supported LoRa board, and a band-matched antenna. Firmware and regional settings must match the hardware and local rules.

changes.before: A hyper-local mesh node. Sunlight in, encrypted packets out, no license and no bill.
changes.after: A mesh node. Sunlight in, short encrypted messages out.

changes.before: The inverter trap versus the DC-native protocol: the conventional chain loses 10 to 15 percent converting DC to AC and again converting back to DC at the wall brick, while the DC-native chain runs solar to battery to fuse block to devices with zero conversion loss
changes.after: Two power paths: an inverter and wall adapter convert DC to AC and back; a DC distribution path avoids that pair but still has charging, wiring, and voltage-conversion losses.

changes.before: The round-trip toll. Every load in the shell already wanted DC; the inverter chain charges you twice to deliver it.
changes.after: The round-trip toll. When a load already wants DC, the inverter chain charges you twice to deliver it.

changes.before: The Neighborhood Fab Lab. Broken means fabricate, not wait.
changes.after: The neighborhood fab lab. Broken means fabricate, not wait.

changes.before: Sunrise from orbit. The new era does not ask permission.
changes.after: Sunrise from orbit. The new era doesn't ask permission, and it still has work to do.

changes.before: A homemade cyberdeck: rugged case, mechanical keyboard, amber map screen, antenna
changes.after: A homemade cyberdeck: a rugged hard case holding a mechanical keyboard, an amber map-lit screen, and a stub antenna
